sections.h2: Where is New Milford, and why is it unusual among Connecticut towns?
sections.html:
New Milford is a town in Litchfield County, about 14 miles north of Danbury on the Housatonic River, and it is the largest town in Connecticut by land area. The Census Bureau lists 61.6 square miles of land, with Greenwich in second place at 47.62 square miles in total area.

The town is part of Greater Danbury and the New York metropolitan area, roughly 50 miles west of Hartford and 63 miles northeast of New York City. The 2020 census counted 28,115 residents, and the 2024 estimate shown on Wikipedia is 28,334.

A town this large has long drives between its parts, and a house on a farm road in Merryall is a very different sale from one near the town green.

sections.h2: What are the villages and areas of New Milford?
sections.html:
New Milford has no single neighborhood system. It has named communities and districts spread across the town: New Milford Center, Gaylordsville, Northville, Still River, Lanesville, Merryall (upper and lower), Merwinsville, Chimney Point, Park Lane, Candlewood Hills, Sunny Valley, Pickett District and Squash Hollow.

  • Gaylordsville has its own ZIP code, 06755, and the rest of town uses 06776.
  • The town's roads largely branch off U.S. 7 and U.S. 202, which cross and split inside New Milford.
  • Communities on the northeast corner of Candlewood Lake and the rural land between Routes 7 and 202 see more visitors from May to October.

Knowing which of these areas your house is in helps buyers picture the commute and the setting.

sections.h2: What is the history of New Milford?
sections.html:
John Noble Sr. and his eight-year-old daughter Sarah were the first English settlers in 1707, and the town was incorporated in 1712. Before that, the Wawyachtonoc people farmed and fished along the Housatonic and Still rivers.

Through the 19th century the town made buttons, hats, furniture, pottery, lime and paint, and tobacco became the major crop. Several tobacco warehouses survive and are on the National Register of Historic Places, including the Schoverling warehouse on Wellsville Avenue and the Wildman warehouse on Bridge Street. Buck's Rock Camp was founded in 1942 and still operates.

The New Milford Center Historic District, covering Bennitt, Elm, East, South Main, Mill and Railroad streets, is also on the National Register, so some of the housing near the green is genuinely old.

sections.h2: How do Candlewood Lake and the rivers affect a New Milford property?
sections.html:
New Milford sits on the northeastern shore of Candlewood Lake, and the East Aspetuck, Still and Housatonic rivers all flow through town. Several local offices handle questions that come up around water.

  • The Candlewood Lake Authority has a listed office at 860-354-6928.
  • The Inland Wetlands office is at 860-355-6083.
  • The Health Department and sanitarian can be reached at 860-355-6035, which matters for septic questions.

If your house is near wetlands, a river or the lake, ask these offices what a buyer would need to know.

sections.h2: What is the climate like, and what does it do to a house?
sections.html:
New Milford has a humid continental climate with mild to warm summers, cold winters and precipitation spread evenly through the year, about 52.95 inches in total. The Candlelight Farms Airport station records a mean January high of 36 degrees and a mean July high of 85.

The record low is minus 18 degrees from January 1968, and the record high is 103 from July 1966. Snowfall in winter is generally frequent, so roofs, heating and driveways take a beating.

An aging oil or propane system, a roof past its life or a wet basement are the repairs that tend to come up in a Litchfield County sale, and a buyer paying cash will not ask you to fix them first.

sections.h2: What local services and offices should a New Milford seller know?
sections.html:
New Milford's town hall lists a full directory of departments, and several are useful before a sale.

The Town Clerk records the deed, and the Tax Collector can tell you your balance. The town government is a mayor-council system with a nine-member Town Council. The town has also built a 1,000,000-gallon sewer plant expansion on West Street, and the WPCA can tell you whether your address is on sewer.

sections.h2: How are New Milford property taxes handled when you sell?
sections.html:
Connecticut towns bill property tax under state law, and a seller normally settles the tax balance through the closing.

Newtown's Tax Collector cites a state statute, CGS 12-146, that charges 18 percent annual interest on late municipal tax, or 1.5 percent per month with a $2 minimum per installment. Whether New Milford follows the same installment calendar is a question for its Tax Collector.

The Assessor at 860-355-6070 handles questions about your assessed value.

sections.h2: What conveyance tax applies to a New Milford sale?
sections.html:
The State of Connecticut charges a conveyance tax on each deed, and the seller side handles the return. The base is three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-quarter of one percent to the municipality.

  • A residential price above $800,000 is charged a higher state rate on the excess.
  • Form OP-236 is filed with the town clerk at recording, and the tax is paid then.
  • Targeted investment communities may add up to one-quarter of one percent.

For a $350,000 house the base tax would be $3,500. Ask the New Milford Town Clerk to confirm the rate for your sale.

sections.h2: How do commuting and schools affect New Milford sales?
sections.html:
New Milford is served by Housatonic Area Regional Transit bus routes, and U.S. 7 and U.S. 202 are the main highways. Metro-North's Danbury Branch ends at Danbury, and the tracks north of Danbury currently carry freight only, though extending passenger service has been discussed for years.

The New Milford School District runs Hill and Plain and Northville elementary schools, Sarah Noble Intermediate School, Schaghticoke Middle School and New Milford High School. Canterbury School, a Catholic boarding school, is also in town.

sections.h2: What are your options for selling a New Milford house?
sections.html:
Owners usually weigh a traditional listing against a direct cash sale, and the right choice depends on condition and timing.

  • With a listing, expect showings, a buyer's inspection and possibly lender-driven repair requests.
  • With a cash sale, you can skip repairs and choose a closing date.
  • An inherited or rural house that needs work often fits the second route.

faqs.q: Is New Milford the largest town in Connecticut?
faqs.a: Yes, by land area. It has about 61.6 square miles of land, more than any other Connecticut town, according to Census Bureau figures cited on Wikipedia.

faqs.q: How do I find out my New Milford tax balance before closing?
faqs.a: Call the Tax Collector at 860-355-6085. The office can give the amount owed so it is handled at the closing.

faqs.q: Is there a conveyance tax when I sell a New Milford house?
faqs.a: Yes. The base rate is three-quarters of one percent to the state and one-quarter of one percent to the town. The Town Clerk can confirm whether any extra municipal rate applies.

faqs.q: Can I sell a lakeside house near Candlewood Lake as-is?
faqs.a: Yes. A cash buyer purchases the property in its current condition. The Candlewood Lake Authority and the Inland Wetlands office can answer questions about waterfront rules.
The New Milford School District operates Hill and Plain, Northville, Sarah Noble Intermediate, Schaghticoke Middle and New Milford High School.

faqs.q: Is there commuter rail in New Milford?
faqs.a: No. The Metro-North Danbury Branch ends in Danbury, and the tracks north of there are used by the Housatonic Railroad for freight. Local buses are run by Housatonic Area Regional Transit.
